sents.text: Welcome back.
Today you set up step one of your workbench: Google Colab, connected to Google Drive.
By the end of this lesson, you'll have run your first Python code, and saved your work somewhere that remembers it.
Google Colab is a free service from Google that runs Python in your web browser.
You write code in a notebook, press run, and Google's computers do the work.
Nothing to install, and it works on almost any computer.
All you need is a Google account.
A notebook is a page made of cells.
Code cells hold Python that you can run, one cell at a time.
Text cells hold notes and headings, so your code explains itself.
Run a cell, and its result appears right underneath.
That's why data scientists love notebooks: the code, the results and the story sit together.
Now here's the catch that trips up almost every beginner.
The computer Colab gives you is temporary.
Leave it idle, or keep it running for many hours, and Colab takes it back.
Any file you saved on that computer disappears with it.
So the golden rule is simple: anything you want to keep goes into Google Drive.
Here's what we'll set up together.
First, a folder in your Google Drive called workbench.
Second, a notebook saved inside it.
Third, a connection from the notebook to your Drive, so code can read and save files there.
Do these three things once, and every lab in this course starts from the same place.
